---
title: "Summarize groups"
---

This example computes a count, a total, and a mean for each region and sorts
the regions by their totals.

Prerequisites: PHP 8.3 or later and `composer require phpstats/phplyr`. The pipe version needs PHP 8.5. See [Installation](../getting-started.qmd#installation).

The sales table is created inline. Save the script as `example.php` in the
project directory and run `php example.php`.

{{< include pages/_group-and-summarize.md >}}

`group_by('region')` makes each region a group, and `summarize()` returns one
row per group with a column for each named argument. `n()` counts the rows in
the group. The South region has a missing `units` value, so `naRm: true`
leaves it out of the sum and the mean, as R's `na.rm = TRUE` does. Without
it, both would be NA. `arrange(desc('total_units'))` sorts the summary from
the largest total to the smallest.

Each argument of `summarize()` can use the columns created before it. A
summary named `units` would replace the `units` column for the arguments
after it, as in dplyr, which is why the total is called `total_units`.

See [Single-table functions](../reference/single-table.qmd#summaries) for `summarize()`,
[Grouping](../reference/grouping.qmd) for `group_by()`, and
[Vector helpers](../reference/vectors.qmd#summaries) for `n()`, `sum()`, and
`mean()`.
